threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'bus stop' instead of 'the bus stop,' and your bag isn’t full of random takeaway menus from all the local spots.
Caught a late 333 and overheard a couple arguing about their takeaway order. Turns out he forgot the garlic bread—it's always the small things, innit?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy riding his bike home with a tree on his shoulder, like it was just a normal day. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24-hour Turkish döner shop where the same guy has been flipping meat since the early 90s, still remembers regulars by name.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they roll their eyes at the BART delays but still hit up the taqueria after a late night out, no matter what.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy dressed as a dinosaur calmly waiting for the bus at Turk and Leavenworth. Only in SF do we treat Muni delays like a costume party.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the tiny bars and local plazas where real life unfolds, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their unworn sneakers and the way they still pull out a map in the streets, looking lost.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses are 'on time' instead of just 'not late enough to walk.'
Caught a night bus home from Brixton and overheard a couple arguing over who was to blame for the broken heating. Classic late-night drama!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One rainy morning, I saw a guy selling homemade soup from his window, offering bowls to drenched passersby. That's when it hit me: this place has a heart.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that serves its own homemade hot sauce—so fiery, it has a warning sign. A true rite of passage!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they fist-bump the guy sweeping the sidewalks at 16th and Mission, not just ignore them like tourists do.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at Civic Center today just as someone was arguing with a dog about who's getting off first. The dog's winning, obviously.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve tapas, but many locals prefer their 'pintxos'—tiny snacks skewered with a toothpick. It's a whole different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment in the Mercat de la Llibertat, staring at the variety of sausages like they've just landed on another planet.
